_what: The thruster allocation matrix the DEPLOYED policy actually trained with, copied here verbatim so the board can verify its own deployment constants without reaching the training host. This file is the ARTIFACT, not a constant: it is the only thing that answers 'what did this checkpoint learn'. A source-tree constant (_ESC_CHANNEL_ORDER and friends) cannot answer that and produced four wrong thruster_order values in a row.
_when_to_update: Only when a NEW checkpoint is packed onto the board. Re-copy from that run's params/env.yaml and update provenance in the same edit. If you find yourself editing thruster_order without touching this file, stop -- one of the two is wrong.

allocation_matrix._cols: sim action index 0..5 (action[2:8] of the 8D action)

geometry._note: Used to invert M = r x F onto a discrete position grid. From actuators.xacro; reproduces the matrix above to four decimals.

measured_channel_map._frame: GRIPPER = 12 o'clock, looking DOWN at the robot from above. +x = 3 o'clock, +y = 12 o'clock, +z = up (right-handed). EVERY azimuth in this file is on this clock face and no other.
measured_channel_map._why_the_frame_line_exists: The 2026-07-05 B1 record said m1=rear-left, m2=front-left, m4=front-right, m5=rear-right without naming its 'front'. It is correct, but only readable once you know its front was the 6 o'clock side (opposite the gripper) with left=3 o'clock. Not stating the frame cost hours and made two correct measurements look like they contradicted each other. State the frame or the record is unusable.
measured_channel_map._measured: b1_channel_probe.py, dry, one channel at a time. Independently agreed by the 2026-07-05 B1 record (once re-framed), the 2026-08-11 probe, and a 2026-08-12 re-probe of m1 and m2.

measured_thruster_sign._what: SIGN of the yaw/attitude response to a POSITIVE command on each firmware channel, measured in the tank 2026-08-12 with b1_channel_probe.py (mixer bypassed, one channel at a time, level 0.25 -- 0.05 is inside the 1450-1545 ESC deadband and spins nothing).
measured_thruster_sign._how_to_read_it: Judge from the GYRO_Z BURST TRACE, not from a mean delta over the drive window: the robot is free-floating, so drift contaminates any average, and a faulty channel that bites intermittently averages to noise. m4 looked like noise until the per-sample trace was read.

m0.basis: CONFIRMED, two independent lines. (a) +0.25 -> pitch -3.36 deg (3 o'clock rises) and -0.25 -> pitch +1.15 deg, a clean reversal with roll unchanged (no Mx, as expected for a thruster on the x axis). (b) operator observed the robot DESCEND on the -0.25 run -- downward thrust for a negative command, so positive = up. Sim col3 (Fz +1.0, My -0.145) also puts +x up for a positive action. All three agree.

m1.basis: +0.25 -> gyro_z positive on 64/74 drive samples, peak +1.296 rad/s, net +62.4. Saturated and unambiguous.

m5.basis: +0.25 -> gyro_z negative on 64/74 samples, peak -1.267 rad/s, net -64.2.

m4.basis: Faulty -- see status. It only produces thrust for a NEGATIVE command: -0.90 gave a sustained burst (76/96 samples, peak +0.278 rad/s, net +9.7) while +0.90 gave essentially nothing (peak -0.057). Extrapolating, a positive command would be -yaw, i.e. OPPOSITE m1. All five m4 runs agree in direction (+0.25 -> -4.5 deg, +0.50 -> -1.9, -0.50 -> +3.2, -0.90 -> +yaw). RE-MEASURE AFTER REPAIR before trusting this.

measured_thruster_sign._discriminator_result: m4 is the ONLY channel where the sim TAM and the firmware yaw PID disagree. Sim maps m4 -> col5 (Mz +0.144, SAME sign as m1); firmware pid.cpp:22-25 has m1 = +PID_yaw but m4 = -PID_yaw (OPPOSITE). The provisional measurement above favours the FIRMWARE, i.e. the sim TAM is wrong for m4 as well as for the verticals. m1, m2 and m5 cannot discriminate -- both sources predict + - - and both are right.

_expected_thruster_order_note: DERIVED, not chosen: test_deploy_constants.py recomputes it from allocation_matrix + measured_channel_map and asserts it equals both this field and thruster_mixer.DEFAULT_ORDER. Three-way agreement or the test fails.

open.thruster_sign: UNMEASURED. Matching by position puts an Mz sign on each corner opposite to the 2026-07-05 rotation record (m1,m4 = CW; m2,m5 = CCW). A permutation cannot flip a sign; the per-channel sign table can, and a solution provably exists because each horizontal thruster is tangential to its own radius. Restrained-tank measurement, Phase 2b-0, m0 first. Cannot be measured dry.
open.sim_tam_is_rotated: The sim's horizontal columns sit 90 deg from the real robot and its two vertical columns are swapped, which is why thruster_order is not identity. The vertical half is acknowledged upstream: constrained-albc 3bb042b says 'STILL OPEN ... vertical Fz/My row redesign'. The permanent fix is to correct the sim TAM and retrain; until then the mixer bridges it.
